visual_goal: Show events leaving services only through the outbox, travelling on keyed topics, reaching partners only through a filtering gateway, with webhooks as the fast path and the feed and reconciliation as the guarantee.
prompt: A left-to-right architecture illustration. Far left: a stack of generic service boxes labeled 'Producing services'. Right of it, a tray-shaped table labeled 'Outbox'. In the center, a set of parallel horizontal pipes labeled 'Topics'. Above-right of the pipes, a group of three small consumer boxes labeled 'Internal consumers'. Below-right of the pipes, a filter gate labeled 'Event gateway'. Right of the gate, two outputs: above, a mailbox with a stack of envelopes labeled 'Event feed'; below, a bell labeled 'Webhooks'. Far right, generic partner buildings labeled 'Partners'. Bottom left, a balance-scale box labeled 'Reconciliation'. Arrows: one arrow from 'Producing services' to 'Outbox' labeled 'one transaction'; one arrow from 'Outbox' to 'Topics' labeled 'at least once'; one arrow from 'Topics' to 'Internal consumers'; one arrow from 'Topics' to 'Event gateway'; one arrow from 'Event gateway' to 'Event feed'; one arrow from 'Event gateway' to 'Webhooks'; one arrow from 'Webhooks' to 'Partners' labeled 'signed'; one dashed arrow from 'Partners' to 'Event feed' labeled 'replay'; one arrow from 'Reconciliation' up into 'Topics' labeled 'corrective events'.
alt: Producing services write events to an outbox in one transaction; events travel at least once onto topics, which feed internal consumers and an event gateway; the gateway feeds an event feed and signed webhooks to partners, who can replay from the feed; reconciliation emits corrective events onto the topics.

visual_goal: Show a webhook subscription as a stateful object: active, failing, disabled after 72 hours, replaying when re-enabled, back to active once caught up, and suspended when authorization is revoked.
prompt: A simple state map of five rounded tiles arranged in a loop. Left: green 'Active'. Top right: orange 'Failing'. Right: red 'Disabled'. Bottom right: teal 'Replaying'. Far bottom left, set apart: grey 'Suspended'. Exactly six arrows: one from 'Active' to 'Failing' labeled 'delivery fails'; one from 'Failing' back to 'Active' labeled 'succeeds'; one from 'Failing' to 'Disabled' labeled '72 hours'; one from 'Disabled' to 'Replaying' labeled 're-enabled'; one from 'Replaying' to 'Active' labeled 'caught up'; one from 'Active' down to 'Suspended' labeled 'access revoked'. A small stopwatch icon on the '72 hours' arrow and a small rewind icon inside 'Replaying'.
alt: A webhook subscription moves from Active to Failing when delivery fails and back when it succeeds; after 72 hours of failure it is Disabled; when re-enabled it Replays and returns to Active once caught up; revoked access moves it to Suspended.

visual_goal: Show the odometer correction replayed on the backbone: internal consumers re-derive, the gateway asks Charter which clients received the facts, and only those clients get a thin webhook and re-fetch at no charge.
prompt: A left-to-right swimlane illustration with six vertical lanes, each with one thin vertical lifeline running down from the center of its heading, and each heading a small icon with a label, in this order from left to right: a history folder labeled 'Tracewell', three small boxes labeled 'Internal consumers', parallel pipes labeled 'Topics', a filter gate labeled 'Event gateway', a stamp-and-ledger labeled 'Charter', and a generic office computer labeled 'Data client'. Every arrow starts exactly on the sender's lifeline and ends exactly on the receiver's lifeline. Horizontal message arrows from top to bottom: one arrow from 'Tracewell' rightward across to 'Topics' labeled '2870 corrections'; one arrow from 'Topics' leftward to 'Internal consumers' labeled 're-derive'; one arrow from 'Topics' rightward to the adjacent 'Event gateway' labeled 'same events'; one arrow from 'Event gateway' to 'Charter' labeled 'who received?'; one return arrow from 'Charter' to 'Event gateway' labeled '19 clients'; one arrow from 'Event gateway' to 'Data client' labeled 'thin webhook'; one arrow from 'Data client' back to 'Event gateway' labeled 're-fetch'; one final green arrow from 'Event gateway' to 'Data client' labeled 'no charge'.
alt: Swimlanes: Tracewell publishes 2870 corrections onto topics; internal consumers re-derive; the event gateway asks Charter who received the facts, gets 19 clients, sends each a thin webhook, and the client re-fetches at no charge.
